subject: General Knowledge
description: Covers World Environment, Water, Earth, Yoga, Human Rights, and Democracy days.

questions.stem: World Environment Day is celebrated globally every year on:

options.option_text: June 5
April 22
March 21
September 16

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: World Environment Day (WED) is celebrated annually on June 5. This date was chosen by the United Nations to mark the first day of the landmark 1972 Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment (which also led to the creation of UNEP).
DECOY BUSTING: April 22 is Earth Day (focused on the modern environmental movement starting in 1970 in the US). March 21 is the International Day of Forests. September 16 is World Ozone Day (commemorating the signing of the Montreal Protocol).
EXAM INSIGHT: Every year, WED has a different host country and a specific theme. For example, in 2018, India hosted WED with the theme "Beat Plastic Pollution." Remembering the dates of major environmental days is a guaranteed mark in SSC and State PSC objective papers.

questions.stem: Which date is observed as 'World Water Day' by the United Nations to highlight the importance of fresh water?

options.option_text: March 22
April 22
May 22
February 2

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: World Water Day is held annually on 22 March. It was first proposed in Agenda 21 at the 1992 UN Conference on Environment and Development (Earth Summit) in Rio de Janeiro. The day focuses on advocating for the sustainable management of freshwater resources and tackling the global water crisis (SDG 6).
DECOY BUSTING: A useful mnemonic for the 22nd of spring months: 
- March 22 = World Water Day
- April 22 = Earth Day
- May 22 = International Day for Biological Diversity.
February 2 is World Wetlands Day (marking the adoption of the Ramsar Convention in 1971).
EXAM INSIGHT: Water scarcity is a critical issue for India (which has 18% of the global population but only 4% of fresh water). Questions often link World Water Day to government initiatives like the Jal Jeevan Mission.

questions.stem: The United Nations celebrates 'International Yoga Day' globally on June 21. Why was this specific date chosen?

options.option_text: It is the Summer Solstice in the Northern Hemisphere, the longest day of the year, carrying special significance in yogic tradition
It marks the birthday of the ancient sage Patanjali, the compiler of the Yoga Sutras
It is the anniversary of Swami Vivekananda's historic speech at the World Parliament of Religions in Chicago
It was the date when the Ministry of AYUSH was officially formed in India

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: During his address to the UN General Assembly in 2014 proposing the day, PM Narendra Modi suggested June 21 because it is the Summer Solstice. It is the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere and holds special significance in many parts of the world. In yogic lore, the first full moon after summer solstice is Guru Purnima, when Shiva (the first yogi or Adiyogi) began imparting the knowledge of yoga to the Saptarishis.
DECOY BUSTING: Patanjali's exact birthdate is unknown. Swami Vivekananda's Chicago speech was on September 11, 1893. National Youth Day (Jan 12) is celebrated on Vivekananda's birthday.
EXAM INSIGHT: The UNGA adopted the resolution for International Yoga Day in December 2014 with a record 177 co-sponsoring nations. The first Yoga Day was celebrated in 2015.

options.option_text: Human Rights Day
World AIDS Day
International Anti-Corruption Day
World Health Day

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Human Rights Day is observed every year on 10 December. This is the day the United Nations General Assembly adopted, in 1948, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR). The UDHR is a milestone document proclaiming the inalienable rights that everyone is entitled to as a human being.
DECOY BUSTING: World AIDS Day is December 1. International Anti-Corruption Day is December 9. World Health Day is April 7 (marking the founding of the WHO in 1948).
EXAM INSIGHT: The Nobel Peace Prize is traditionally awarded in Oslo, Norway, exactly on December 10 every year to commemorate the death anniversary of Alfred Nobel. This creates a powerful thematic overlap between peace and human rights.

questions.stem: Which day is designated by the UN as the International Day of Democracy?

options.option_text: September 15
January 26
July 4
October 24

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: In 2007, the United Nations General Assembly resolved to observe 15 September as the International Day of Democracy. The purpose is to promote and uphold the principles of democracy and review the state of democracy in the world.
DECOY BUSTING: January 26 is India's Republic Day. July 4 is American Independence Day. October 24 is United Nations Day (the anniversary of the entry into force of the UN Charter in 1945).
EXAM INSIGHT: In India, September 15 is also celebrated as Engineer's Day to mark the birth anniversary of Sir M. Visvesvaraya, one of India's greatest engineers and nation-builders.

questions.stem: World Tuberculosis Day is observed on March 24 each year. The date specifically commemorates which landmark event in the history of medical science?

options.option_text: Founding of the WHO Stop TB Partnership in Geneva, Switzerland in 2001
Dr. Robert Koch's public announcement of isolating the tuberculosis bacillus, 1882
First successful BCG vaccine trial conducted by Calmette and Guérin in 1921
First global TB eradication conference convened in London in the year 1904

questions.explanation: B is correct because on March 24, 1882, Dr. Robert Koch announced to the Berlin Physiological Society that he had isolated Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the causative agent of TB — a discovery that won him the 1905 Nobel Prize in Medicine. Option C is wrong because the BCG vaccine (Bacille Calmette-Guérin) was developed in 1921 but has no link to the March 24 date. Option A is wrong because the Stop TB Partnership was launched in 2001, not in 1882.

questions.stem: Which United Nations health observance day falls on May 31 each year, first established by the World Health Assembly in 1987 under resolution WHA40.38?

options.option_text: World Blood Donor Day — dedicated to voluntary unpaid blood donation
World Heart Day — raising awareness of cardiovascular disease globally
World No Tobacco Day — calling for abstinence from all tobacco products
World Asthma Day — focusing on asthma awareness and management globally

questions.explanation: C is correct because the World Health Assembly designated May 31 as World No Tobacco Day in 1987 to draw attention to the health risks of tobacco and advocate for effective policies. Option A is wrong because World Blood Donor Day is observed on June 14, not May 31. Option B is wrong because World Heart Day falls on September 29.

questions.stem: World Population Day is observed on July 11 each year. The Governing Council of UNDP recommended this date in 1989 to mark which specific demographic milestone?

options.option_text: The world population reaching the 5-billion mark on July 11, 1987
The establishment of the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) in 1969
The adoption of the Bucharest World Population Plan of Action in 1974
The opening of the first International Population Conference in Rome, 1954

questions.explanation: A is correct because July 11, 1987 was dubbed 'Five Billion Day' when the global population symbolically crossed the 5-billion mark; UNDP's Governing Council formalised the observance in 1989 to focus attention on population issues. Option B is wrong because UNFPA was established in 1969 but this date does not fall on July 11. Option C is wrong because the Bucharest Plan of Action was adopted in August 1974, not July 11.

questions.stem: World Food Day is celebrated on October 16 each year. This date was chosen to commemorate the founding anniversary of a UN specialized body. Which agency, and in which year was it established?

options.option_text: World Food Programme (WFP), established in Rome during the year 1961
UN Committee on World Food Security, established in Rome during 1974
International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), created in 1977
Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), established on October 16, 1945

questions.explanation: D is correct because the FAO was formally established on October 16, 1945, in Quebec City, Canada; World Food Day was proclaimed by the FAO Conference in 1979 to mark this anniversary. Option A is a common trap — WFP is the operational food agency often confused with FAO but was founded in 1961. Option C is wrong because IFAD, while food-related, was created in 1977 with no link to October 16.

questions.stem: The UN's International Day for the Eradication of Poverty is observed on October 17. The choice of this date is rooted in a 1987 public gathering that honoured victims of extreme poverty. Where was this historic gathering held?

options.option_text: UN General Assembly Hall, United Nations Headquarters, New York City
Trocadéro, Paris — site of the 1987 gathering honouring victims of poverty
Palais des Nations, Geneva, headquarters of the UN Office at Geneva
Copenhagen, Denmark, venue of the 1995 World Summit on Social Development

questions.explanation: B is correct because on October 17, 1987, Father Joseph Wresinski led over 100,000 people at the Trocadéro in Paris — site of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights signing — to honour victims of poverty and violence; the UN General Assembly officially proclaimed this date in 1992 via resolution 47/196. Option D is a strong distractor because the 1995 Copenhagen Social Summit is genuinely linked to poverty eradication but has no connection to October 17.

questions.stem: UN General Assembly resolution A/RES/77/161 (December 2022) proclaimed March 30 as the International Day of Zero Waste. Which two UN bodies were specifically designated to jointly facilitate its annual observance?

options.option_text: UNDP (New York) and UNIDO (Vienna), focusing on industrial sustainability
FAO (Rome) and IFAD (Rome), emphasizing agricultural waste reduction goals
UNEP (Nairobi) and UN-Habitat (Nairobi), co-facilitating waste governance
WHO (Geneva) and UNCTAD (Geneva), linking health and trade-waste nexus

questions.explanation: C is correct because resolution A/RES/77/161 explicitly tasked UNEP (United Nations Environment Programme) and UN-Habitat (United Nations Human Settlements Programme) — both headquartered in Nairobi — to facilitate the International Day of Zero Waste, reflecting the link between urban settlements and solid-waste management. Option A is wrong because UNIDO's mandate is industrial development, and it was not named in the resolution. Option B is wrong because FAO and IFAD focus on food and agriculture, not municipal solid waste.

questions.stem: The UN General Assembly resolution A/RES/65/5 (October 2010) established World Interfaith Harmony Week during the first week of February. The initiative was originally proposed at the 65th UNGA session by the head of state of which country?

options.option_text: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, represented by then Crown Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz
Sultanate of Oman, championed by Sultan Qaboos bin Said Al Said at UNGA
State of Qatar, proposed by Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani
Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, proposed by King Abdullah II at the 65th UNGA

questions.explanation: D is correct because King Abdullah II of Jordan, known for his inter-religious dialogue initiatives including the 2004 Amman Message, formally proposed World Interfaith Harmony Week at the 65th UN General Assembly in 2010; the resolution was adopted unanimously. Option A is a plausible trap because Saudi Arabia hosts key Islamic holy sites and is often associated with religious diplomacy, but it was not the proposing nation. Options B and C are Gulf-region distractors that test whether candidates confuse Jordanian leadership with broader Arab League interlocutors.
